From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.inference.com>

Subject: Post-call: Exec recap & procurement path for AuroraMed

Hi Emily —

Thanks again for taking time today — great conversation with you and the care ops team. Quick executive-level recap and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned: 

High-level pain points discussed:
- Latency for real-time triage: current on-prem pipeline suffers from 800–1200ms per request at peak, causing delayed clinician workflows.
- Cost unpredictability and administrative overhead for model serving across clinics.
- Data residency and HIPAA controls: need private VPC or dedicated environment, logging/audit requirements.

Goals / business outcomes you emphasized:
- Reduce inference latency to under 200ms P95 for triage use case to speed decisioning at point-of-care.
- Cut per-inference cost by ~40% through smarter batching and caching to enable broader rollout across 30 clinics.
- Provide a private deployment option (VPC or on-prem) with KMS integration and audit logs for compliance.
- Achieve a pilot ROI within 3–4 months of go-live.

Procurement path & timeline (as we understand it):
- Security review (SOC 2 + architecture diagram) -> Legal terms review -> Procurement approval -> Pilot (canary) -> Full rollout.
- Suggested milestone: security docs by 2/24, commercial terms by 3/5, procurement sign-off target by 3/12.

Action items / next steps (owners):
1) Aditya (me) — share MAP (migration & pilot plan) and line-item pricing for pilot and annual committed capacity (attached).
2) AuroraMed — share procurement contact + preferred contract template; confirm internal timeline.
3) Redwood (Marissa) — prepare SOC 2 attestation and architecture diagram for security review.
4) Schedule a 30-minute procurement + security sync w/ Carlos and our legal/security leads next week.

Attachments: AuroraMed-MAP.pdf (application/pdf), redwood-pricing-2026.xlsx (spreadsheet)

If that matches your view, I’ll loop in procurement and propose a calendar invite for the security sync.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this forward.

Best,
Aditya Rao

Subject: Internal: AuroraMed exec recap + escalation items

Team — quick internal note to summarize the thread for leadership and flag escalation items: 

Summary (for the exec deck):
- AuroraMed is a high-priority HS account: they need sub-200ms P95 latency and a private deployment option for PHI. The pilot is for 30 clinics with a clear path to enterprise rollout (~12–18 months). Expected business outcome: faster triage, fewer manual referrals, and ~$1.2M ARR opportunity in 18 months if pilot succeeds.

Escalation / risk items:
- InfoSec requires SOC 2 Type II, architecture diagram, and data flow mapping. This is gating for security review and procurement schedule.
- Pricing sensitivity: procurement will expect clear pilot pricing and a predictable committed-capacity model. We should be prepared to offer a limited pilot discount and a clear conversion path to dedicated capacity.
- Contract terms: AuroraMed will push on data residency and indemnity clauses; legal should be primed for a short negotiation cycle.

Proposed next steps (owners & timeline):
- Aditya: send updated MAP + itemized pilot pricing and SOW draft by EOD 2/20 (owner: Aditya).
- Marissa: upload SOC 2 Type II report, architecture diagrams, and customer reference list to the shared Drive folder and share link with Carlos by 2/24 (owner: Marissa).
- Laura: coordinate legal to pre-review AuroraMed RFP and surface any non-starters by 2/27 (owner: Laura).

- Set procurement + security sync with Carlos for week of 2/24; propose 2/25 10:00 AM PT (Aditya to confirm).

Commercial recommendation for execs: offer a 6-week pilot on Dedicated capacity with a 30% pilot discount and option to convert to 12-month committed capacity at a blended rate. This reduces procurement friction and preserves an upgrade path.
